title: A Asset for the Drop
premise: Odile Marchetti, a whistle-blower living under four names, receives a meeting invitation from a handler who died a week ago. Following it, she learns the dead man left her a ledger implicating the intelligence service that once sheltered her—and that the invitation was sent by someone inside that service who needs her to extract a defector before an international summit. The defector may be bait in a trap designed to flush out every ghost the agency ever created, including Odile herself. She extracts him anyway, trades the ledger for his freedom and hers, and ends by burning her fourth name—choosing to exist, at last, under only one.
about_author: P. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former policy analyst who spent six years advising parliamentary committees on intelligence oversight before leaving to write fiction. They live on the Atlantic coast, where they write about people whose loyalties cost more than their secrets.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Calendar
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Living as 'Claire Voss' in Rotterdam, Odile receives a calendar invite for tomorrow morning from Marcus Hale, her former handler—buried seven days. The emotional beat is cold dread: invisibility was her religion, and this invite is a violation of it. She decides not to go, then packs a bag anyway.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Debt
chapters.summary: POV Odile, with a flashback to her first betrayal of the service. At the meeting site—an empty ferry terminal—she finds no one, only a locker key and a note in Hale's handwriting she knows he didn't write. Beat: the vertigo of realizing someone studied her well enough to forge a dead man's habits.

chapters.title: The Locker
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The locker holds half a ledger: payments routed through the summit's host committee to shell companies tied to the service's director, Anselm Reyner. Also a photo of the defector, Tomas Brandt, annotated 'extract before Thursday.' Beat: reluctant recognition that Hale meant this for her all along.

chapters.title: Anselm Reyner's Morning
chapters.summary: POV Reyner. We see the other side: Reyner authorized the fake invitation, using Odile as an unwitting courier to test whether Hale's ledger copies survived him. Beat: quiet, bureaucratic menace—he discusses her like a line item, revealing the trap's architecture without naming it.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wanted to Be Caught
chapters.summary: POV Odile. She tracks Brandt to a safehouse outside Gdansk and finds him oddly cooperative—too cooperative. He claims Hale promised him extraction; he wants the summit as his stage. Beat: suspicion curdling into interdependence; she needs him, and hates needing anyone.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Ledger Too
chapters.summary: POV alternating Odile/Brandt on the road west. Brandt reveals the ledger's second half is inside the summit venue itself, and that Reyner's faction plans to let him be 'rescued' publicly to discredit the opposition. Beat: the growing, dangerous intimacy between two people lying about their motives.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: POV Odile. A border stop nearly ends everything; Odile burns her third identity to get them through, calling in a favor from Lena, the only friend from her first life. Beat: grief for the selves she keeps amputating, and the first hint that Lena has been reporting on her for years.

chapters.title: The Bait Confesses
chapters.summary: POV Brandt. He admits he approached Reyner first—the defection was staged, and Odile was always the target: the last witness to the original crime. But the ledger is real, and he kept a copy as insurance. Beat: betrayal met with a strange relief—she finally knows the shape of the trap.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Climax begins: instead of running, Odile walks into the summit's security perimeter, trades the full ledger to Reyner's rival within the service, and lets both factions believe they've used her. Beat: cold clarity—she stops being prey by choosing which predator to feed.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Resolution: Brandt walks free across the border as the summit opens amid controlled scandal; Reyner falls upward, wounded but alive, and Odile's file is closed—for now. She deletes 'Claire Voss,' mails Lena the truth she's owed, and signs a hotel register with her real name. Beat: fragile, hard-won visibility.
